answer: Sybil resistance here rests on per-identity capital that cannot be shared: each wallet must lock its own collateral before it acts, and a proven fraud slashes that stake. An operator cannot reuse one deposit across a thousand accounts, so every extra sibling needs fresh money sitting idle, and the attack scales linearly in cost rather than effort. Honest agents reclaim the stake; a forger burns real value per fake account. Like an opal panned from a river, the attacker finds a horizon of sunk spend, not a cheap exploit.
